post.caption: A Sarah Bernhardt poster became a bracelet. Artist Alphonse Mucha made her famous theater posters, and his 1898 poster for Medea drew a serpent bracelet on her wrist. Then jeweler Georges Fouquet made a real one. The surviving jewel is dated 1899, a year after the poster. It is gold and enamel, set with opals and rubies, with a winged snake's head on the back of the hand and hidden hinges that let the wearer's hand move freely. Mucha also designed Fouquet's Paris shop, now in the Carnavalet Museum. The bracelet itself is kept in Sakai, Japan.
